free_tier.stated: Free (up to 5 users): 1 GB LFS storage. Academic 5 GB, Standard 5 GB, Premium 10 GB. Extra storage sold in 100 GB units at $10/month. Notable counter-property: no per-file cap at all.

egress.terms: Not metered — Atlassian publishes no LFS bandwidth quota, only storage in 100 GB units. This is the one LFS host where the storage number is small but the transfer side is genuinely unstated/unbilled.

tooling: git-lfs. Note: SSH not usable for LFS repos? (not stated) — the documented limitation is that repository transfer and forking both break LFS links; the alternative route is `git lfs fetch --all` + `git lfs push --all`.
chaining: 1 GB per free workspace, unlimited free workspaces (each needs an email). 500 workspaces = 500 GB of very awkward storage. Weak: no route to manage many workspaces at once, and the workspace is tied to users.
limits_note: 'there's no limit on the LFS file size you can push to Bitbucket Cloud' — genuinely no per-file cap. Forks do not copy LFS objects (fork points at parent's store, and the fork lacks permission) — so fork-based sharding fails. Repo archives do not include LFS files.

reliability_note: Fork/transfer/archive are all documented as broken for LFS repos, which makes recovery awkward. Storage overage is auto-billed in 100 GB increments rather than blocked.
